newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IEB seeks to set up bank in the Ukraine.
newsitem.headline: IEB seeks to set up bank in the Ukraine.

text.p: Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank (IEB), controlled by Italy's Bancario San Paolo group, said on Friday it would open a representative office in Kiev in March as the first step towards setting up a bank in Ukraine.
IEB officials told a news conference that IEB planned to enter Ukraine's lucrative banking market either by acquiring a local bank or founding a new one.

The plans matched the strategy of San Paolo, which already had representative offices in Poland and Russia and has made concentrated efforts to expand in central and eastern Europe, IEB CEO Pier Franco Rubatto said.
"This is a small step, but may have large perspectives," he said, adding that Ukraine, the second largest country of Europe, offered vast business opportunities as economic growth picked up.

IEB Chairman Laszlo Body said that German, French and Dutch banks were eyeing a share of the potentially lucrative market, where the number of banks dropped to about 180 from 220 last year amid rapid consolidation of the industry.
IEB's potential co-investors included three international groups, all IEB shareholders, and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, Rubatto said.
The three groups, which the IEB office will also represent in Kiev, were San Paolo, the U.K.'s Hambros and Spain's Banco de Santander.
